bodyparts3d.missingFromOfficialRelease: Checked against https://dbarchive.biosciencedbc.jp/data/bodyparts3d/LATEST/isa_parts_list_e.txt (BodyParts3D 4.0): no latissimus dorsi, rectus abdominis, internal oblique, transversus abdominis, quadratus lumborum, masseter, temporalis, pterygoids or facial muscles other than the platysma.

modelled.latissimus-dorsi: Modelled: a sheet from the spinous processes of T7–L5 and the back of the iliac crest to the floor of the intertubercular groove of the humerus, wrapped over the ribs and the deep back muscles of this body (beneath the trapezius); 3–7 mm thick, tapering to its tendon.
modelled.rectus-abdominis: Modelled: a strap about 6–8 mm thick from the pubic crest beside the symphysis to the xiphoid and costal cartilages 5–7 of this body, bowed 3 cm forwards like the abdominal wall; its tendinous intersections are not shown.
modelled.internal-oblique: Modelled: the BodyParts3D external oblique of this body moved 6 mm towards the trunk, trimmed below the 10th rib (the internal oblique reaches the lower three ribs); its fibres run at right angles to the external oblique’s, which the model does not show.
modelled.transversus-abdominis: Modelled: the BodyParts3D external oblique of this body moved 12 mm towards the trunk, trimmed below the 7th costal cartilage (the transversus arises from the inner surfaces of costal cartilages 7–12).
modelled.quadratus-lumborum: Modelled: a slab about 2 cm thick in the posterior abdominal wall of this body, from the back of the iliac crest to the lower border of the 12th rib, against the tips of the L1–L4 transverse processes.
modelled.masseter: Modelled: cast onto the lateral surface of the ramus of this mandible and up to the lower border of the zygomatic arch, 4–11 mm thick.
modelled.temporalis: Modelled: a fan cast onto the temporal fossa of this skull, from the superior temporal line converging beneath the zygomatic arch onto the coronoid process; 3–7 mm thick.
modelled.lateral-pterygoid: Modelled: a tube 11 mm across from the lateral pterygoid plate of this sphenoid to the neck of the mandibular condyle.
modelled.medial-pterygoid: Modelled: a tube about 12 mm across from the pterygoid plates of this sphenoid to the inner surface of the mandibular angle, mirroring the masseter.
modelled.orbicularis-oculi: Modelled: a ring about 42 × 36 mm round the orbital opening, centred on this body’s eyeball (BodyParts3D sclera).
modelled.occipitofrontalis: Modelled: its frontal belly cast onto the frontal bone above the brow and its occipital belly onto the occipital bone above the superior nuchal line, 2.5 mm thick; the epicranial aponeurosis between them is not shown.
modelled.zygomaticus-major: Modelled: a strap from the zygomatic bone of this skull to the corner of the mouth.
modelled.buccinator: Modelled: a sheet cast onto the outer face of the molars and premolars of this body, from behind the second molar to the corner of the mouth.
modelled.orbicularis-oris: Modelled: an oval ring about 54 × 28 mm round the mouth, in front of the incisors of this body.

changesHere: Selected and merged the BodyParts3D muscle meshes listed in src/lab/source/muscles.source.json; welded; simplified with meshoptimizer within 1.2 % relative error (to about a fifth to three fifths of the source triangles: the intercostals and the largest sheets most); subdivided and smoothed the smallest; recomputed smooth normals; translated by the skeleton’s centre offset; modelled the muscles the source lacks on this body’s bones; bound every vertex to its two nearest bones; classified each muscle’s depth.
